name: nyc-taxi-data
what_it_holds: Scripts (R + shell) to download and load 3+ billion NYC taxi and for-hire-vehicle (Uber, Lyft) trip records since 2009 into PostgreSQL or ClickHouse, sourced from official NYC TLC trip-record parquet files (CSV pre-May 2022). TLC records carry pickup/dropoff LocationID fields that include JFK and LaGuardia airport zones, so airport-trip volumes can be isolated. Data not committed to the repo itself (70GB+); pulled via download_raw_data.sh.
why_useful: Directly addresses gap #10 (rail/road/airport ground-travel capacity and traffic) via airport-connection taxi/rideshare volume as a proxy for air-travel demand into NYC, and general rideshare volume as a consumer-travel-strength read.
size_hint: 3B+ trip rows (external); repo itself is code only
license: MIT (code); data is public NYC TLC records
themes: Rail and ground travel: Amtrak ridership, SNCF/DB/Trenitalia open data, Eurostar, bus (FlixBus), rideshare datasets (Uber Movement), NYC TLC airport trips, Chicago taxi
why_all: Directly addresses gap #10 (rail/road/airport ground-travel capacity and traffic) via airport-connection taxi/rideshare volume as a proxy for air-travel demand into NYC, and general rideshare volume as a consumer-travel-strength read.

name: amtrak-data
what_it_holds: Amtrak's monthly performance reports extracted (via Tabula from the published PDFs) into JSON/CSV/XML, organized by year and month, covering five tables per month: Operating Results, Capital Results, Key Performance Indicators, Sources and Uses of Cash, and Route-Level Results. Coverage August 2021 to present (maintainer flags update currency as uncertain); raw PDFs and unprocessed tabula extracts kept under /reports.
why_useful: Directly fills gap #10 (Amtrak/rail traffic) with route-level Amtrak operating and ridership-adjacent metrics at monthly frequency since mid-2021 — the most granular free Amtrak dataset found; useful as a US intercity-rail demand cross-check against ABNB's domestic leisure-travel exposure.
license: not stated in fetch; derived from Amtrak public PDF reports
themes: Rail and ground travel: Amtrak ridership, SNCF/DB/Trenitalia open data, Eurostar, bus (FlixBus), rideshare datasets (Uber Movement), NYC TLC airport trips, Chicago taxi
why_all: Directly fills gap #10 (Amtrak/rail traffic) with route-level Amtrak operating and ridership-adjacent metrics at monthly frequency since mid-2021 — the most granular free Amtrak dataset found; useful as a US intercity-rail demand cross-check against ABNB's domestic leisure-travel exposure.

name: canadian-border-crossings-analysis
what_it_holds: data/ folder with BTS monthly inbound US-Canada land-border crossing counts by port (1996-present), a Border Policy Research Institute passenger-vehicle intercept survey at Whatcom County crossings (31,208 individual responses across 4 waves: Summer 2018, Winter 2019, Summer 2025, Winter 2026), and NTTO air-passenger arrivals data Jan 2019-Jul 2026; scripts/ for the analysis; figures/; MIT license; 15 commits, active through 2026
why_useful: Direct hit on gap 10 (BTS border-crossing data) with committed BTS series plus something we don't hold at all: a point-in-time individual-level cross-border traveler survey (2018-2026, 4 waves) and NTTO air arrivals extending into 2026 — could sharpen the US-Canada leisure travel read for the North America regional split.
geography: US-Canada land border, multiple states/provinces (Vermont, North Dakota, New York, Washington)
themes: Cross-border and visa data: Schengen visa statistics, ESTA, ETIAS, CBP wait times, passport index, border crossings BTS
why_all: Direct hit on gap 10 (BTS border-crossing data) with committed BTS series plus something we don't hold at all: a point-in-time individual-level cross-border traveler survey (2018-2026, 4 waves) and NTTO air arrivals extending into 2026 — could sharpen the US-Canada leisure travel read for the North America regional split.

name: AAAGas
what_it_holds: Python scraper pulling AAA gas prices at metro and state level; metro scrape begins 2024-11-17, state scrape begins the day before (2024-11-16). Includes example plots (Atlanta vs Detroit regular gas). Presumably committed CSVs building daily since Nov 2024, i.e. roughly 2 years of daily state/metro gas price history by the pitch date.
why_useful: Longest-running AAA scrape found (since Nov 2024) -- if the data files are actually committed and current, this is close to a 2-year daily state+metro gas price panel, useful as a proxy for road-trip cost of US domestic travel and regional consumer strength divergence.
time_coverage: Nov 2024 - present (~22 months as of Sep 2026)
size_hint: unknown -- need to check data folder size/row count
themes: Road travel and fuel: gas prices (EIA, AAA), vehicle miles travelled, holiday driving, toll data
why_all: Longest-running AAA scrape found (since Nov 2024) -- if the data files are actually committed and current, this is close to a 2-year daily state+metro gas price panel, useful as a proxy for road-trip cost of US domestic travel and regional consumer strength divergence.

name: Proyecto_Final_ProgramacionII (Costa Rica ICT tourism forecasting)
what_it_holds: data/processed/turismo.csv: cleaned dataset of international tourist arrivals to Costa Rica by country of origin and month, 2019-2025, parsed from data/raw/informes_ict/ (original PDF semi-annual reports from Instituto Costarricense de Turismo, ICT). Uses pdfplumber to extract 'Table 1' (international arrivals by country/month) from each ICT PDF; author states annual totals were validated against ICT's official statistical yearbooks and matched exactly. Also pulls Open-Meteo historical daily temperature for Costa Rica as a weather covariate, aggregated monthly. Includes a trained ML model (not committed, file-size excluded). Course project (BD-143 Programación II), last updated 17 Aug 2026.
why_useful: Direct, verified LatAm regional travel-volume data (gap #7) with a repeatable, source-checked extraction method (ICT PDF -> table) an agent could re-run on newer ICT reports; monthly, by-origin-country granularity is finer than most public Costa Rica tourism series and could proxy US-outbound leisure travel strength relevant to ABNB's LatAm segment.
themes: Caribbean, Central America and island tourism stats (CTO, Costa Rica ICT, Dominican Republic BCRD, Bahamas, Puerto Rico) and Hawaii-like party-size / length-of-stay surveys
why_all: Direct, verified LatAm regional travel-volume data (gap #7) with a repeatable, source-checked extraction method (ICT PDF -> table) an agent could re-run on newer ICT reports; monthly, by-origin-country granularity is finer than most public Costa Rica tourism series and could proxy US-outbound leisure travel strength relevant to ABNB's LatAm segment.
